name: J. M. T. Partello
role: Army lieutenant at Fort Keogh; noted rifle shot
bio: Lieut. J. M. T. Partello of Fort Keogh was praised by the paper as a writer on stock interests and as a marksman. In February 1885 the paper said he was not the author of an alarmist letter on Montana cattle losses, and his letter to A. T. Packard giving the Creedmoor rules was read to the Medora Gun Club, which he later supplied with targets and pasters. In May 1886 the paper reported his perfect score of 15 bull's-eyes at 500 yards with a military rifle.
